title: hometools
description: Types of the hometools package; mise run //home:codegen writes src/hometools/models.py from this file.

Command.description: One hometools command, run by the global mise task of the same purpose.

Bootstrap.description: What bootstrap-toolchain reads: the [vars] versions of the brew packages it must find installed.

llvm.description: TOOLCHAIN_LLVM, [vars] llvm: llvm, lld and lldb.

Verify.description: What toolchain-verify reads: the brew prefix and every [vars] version it checks.

Failure.description: Why a command stopped, printed as one JSON line on stderr.

error.description: The lines the shell task printed, joined by newlines.

DiskSnapshot.description: What disk-snapshot wrote: its folder (none while another run held the lock) and the roots dust did not finish.

folder.description: The new folder under disk-alerts; null when another snapshot held the lock.

timed_out.description: Roots whose dust run was stopped at its time limit; they have no totals.

DiskGuard.description: disk-guard's passing line: the data volume's free space and the floor it cleared.

free_gib.description: Space a normal user can still write on the data volume (f_bavail), in GiB, as monit counts it.

floor_gib.description: The floor: heavy test tasks refuse to start below it.

Writer.description: One process that wrote to disk since the previous disk-log line (proc_pid_rusage, RUSAGE_INFO_V2).

path.description: Its executable (proc_pidpath); empty when it exited before disk-log read it.

written_mib.description: MiB it wrote to disk since the previous line, or since it started when the previous line did not see it.

DiskSample.description: One line of disk-log's samples.jsonl: free space, its drop and the processes that wrote most.

at.description: When disk-log ran, ISO 8601 in UTC.

free_gib.description: Space a normal user can still write on the data volume (f_bavail), in GiB.

drop_gib.description: The previous line's free_gib minus this one's; null on the first line.

writers.description: The processes that wrote most since the previous line, most first.

snapshot.description: The drop reached DROP_GIB, so disk-log started a disk-snapshot.

MonitAlert.description: The last monit alert, as monit-alert writes it to ~/.local/state/dotfiles/monit/alert.json and prints it.

at.description: When monit-alert ran, ISO 8601 in UTC.

service.description: MONIT_SERVICE: the check that fired, such as data or the host name.

event.description: MONIT_EVENT: the kind of event, such as Resource limit matched.

description.description: MONIT_DESCRIPTION: monit's own sentence about the alert.

Result.description: One herdr-doctor check: pass, fail, or unknown when an input it needs could not be read (unknown blocks green).

Window.description: One running Herdr.app process and the HC_SOCKET its environment holds.

hc_socket.description: HC_SOCKET in its environment (sysctl KERN_PROCARGS2), home as ~; null when unset.

Routing.description: A routing input set to a value other than hc's default: it can send a client to another socket.

name.description: HC_SOCKET, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, HC_SESSION, XDG_STATE_HOME, or socket for the config key.

Observation.description: What herdr-doctor read from outside herdr-core: sockets, processes, files and environments, never an hc call.

hc.description: herdr-core's version, from the Info.plist of ~/.local/share/herdr-core/current; null when it is not installed.

app.description: Herdr.app's version, from its Info.plist; null when it is not installed.

skill_tag.description: The herdr-core skill's ref in the skills CLI lock; null when the lock has none.

skills_missing.description: Skill folders (home as ~) with no SKILL.md: herdr-core's, and Claude Code's entries.

cores.description: Core processes: argv hc or herdr-core followed by --hc-launchd or serve (pgrep -f).

listeners.description: The pids holding ~/.local/state/herdr-core/default/default.sock (lsof); empty when it is not a socket.

lock_path.description: The socket path core.lock advertises, home as ~; null when the file is missing.

core_started.description: The one core's start time (ps -o lstart=); null unless exactly one core runs.

windows.description: Each running Herdr.app whose environment could be read.

routing.description: Every routing input set to a value other than the default.

references.description: path:line of each retired-project reference outside the V11 allowlist.

guard.description: What the V15 structural guard found in herdr.py: a named hc program or a process started outside read().

unchanged.description: The socket files, and the core pids when pgrep read them, were the same before and after the doctor's reads.

unknown.description: Inputs not read; each makes the checks needing it unknown unless what was read fails them.

Checks.description: The doctor's checks by ID (docs/designs/herdr-core-socket-cutover.md, The checks).

V1.description: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is absent from a new login shell and from launchctl getenv.

V2.description: No routing input is set in a login shell, launchd, the running app or the herdr-core config.

V3.description: Exactly one process holds the default socket.

V4.description: Exactly one core, it is that holder, and core.lock names the default socket.

V5.description: Nothing holds anything under the old path ~/.local/run/herdr-core.

V7.description: No running Herdr.app has HC_SOCKET in its environment.

V10.description: The herdr-core skill is in all four harness folders at the installed hc's tag.

V11.description: No retired-project reference outside the allowlist.

V15.description: herdr.py names no hc program, only read() starts a process, and the run left cores and sockets as they were.

DoctorReport.description: herdr-doctor's one JSON line: what it read and each check's result.

RollStep.description: One step of the herdr rolling restart (hometools roll <step>, the roll:<step> mise task).

Kind.description: What runs in a terminal: an agent harness whose session can be resumed, or a plain shell.

Role.description: A tab's place in the graph: the one chief of staff, a lead (-lead, -coord or -v2), or a child.

LaneParent.description: A wiki lane page's '## Children' line that names this terminal.

GraphTerminal.description: One terminal of graph.json: its agent, session id, folder and argv when the snapshot ran.

address.description: The hc terminal address, such as t2h4.

session.description: The session id to resume; null for a shell or one not found.

cwd.description: The foreground process's folder, else the terminal's.

lane_parents.description: Lane pages that list it as a child.

is_coordinator.description: It is the chief of staff's terminal.

pid.description: The foreground pid: roll:verify proves an excluded session untouched by it.

kept_from_previous_graph.description: Not live at the snapshot; carried from the previous graph.
Not live at the snapshot; carried from the previous graph.
Not live at the snapshot; carried from the previous graph.

Graph.description: graph.json, which roll:snapshot writes and herdr-startup reads: every space, tab and terminal.

taken_at.description: When the snapshot ran, ISO 8601 with the local offset.

coordinator.description: The chief of staff's terminal, found by name.

WorkElsewhere.description: A session whose checkout is clean while the worktree its lane bullet names has changes.

work_in.description: The worktree with staged or uncommitted changes.

graph.description: graph.json as written; null on a dry run.

graph_copy.description: The timestamped copy beside it; null on a dry run.

agents.description: Live terminals running claude, codex or opencode.

agents_without_session.description: Agent terminals whose session id was not found: they cannot be resumed.

children_without_lane.description: Child Claude tabs no lane page lists.

SessionResult.description: What one step did, or would do, to one session.

terminal.description: The terminal address at the time of the step.

result.description: One word: planned, stopped, started, ok, untouched, or skipped-<why> or failed-<why>.

notes.description: Details: the planned command, jobs found, the check that failed.

Timing.description: How long a roll step waits, in seconds: for a stop-point answer, for an exit or a start, between looks.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for a stop-point answer.

settle.description: Seconds to wait for an exit or a start.

Background.description: What roll:stop found running before /exit, kept in <run>/background/ so it can be re-armed.

jobs.description: Child processes other than MCP servers and language servers, and hc run children that die with it.

footer.description: Claude's 'N in background' footer, when the screen shows one.

exit_dialog.description: The items /exit's 'Background work is running' dialog listed.

worktree.description: Its folder's git status before /exit, for roll:verify; null outside a repository.

Marketplace.description: A Claude plugin marketplace at the snapshot: its GitHub repo and checked-out commit.

repo.description: owner/name from known_marketplaces.json; null when it is not a GitHub source.

head.description: git rev-parse HEAD of its installLocation; null when it is not a git checkout (claude-plugins-official).

Versions.description: <run>/versions.json: what roll:snapshot found installed, so roll:review can pair old with new.

harnesses.description: claude, codex, opencode and agy: the version each one's --version prints; null when it can't run.

plugins.description: Each user-scope plugin id: <version>-<gitCommitSha>, as installed_plugins.json records it.

review.description: <run>/review.md, the source of truth; null on a dry run.

triaged.description: The model triage ran for at least one pair (never for a pair seen before).

gate.description: BREAKING was flagged: roll:all pauses before roll:stop until rerun with --accept-review.

flags.description: Why the gate closed: the triage's BREAKING items, plus the grep's lines when an item went untriaged.

MiseLinks.description: Links under mise's installs folder whose target is missing (reported, never removed).

dangling.description: <tool>/<link> for each dangling link, the global links first.

RollRun.description: One line of ~/.local/state/dotfiles/roll/runs.jsonl: one step of one run.

run.description: The run id, run-<UTC time>-<pid>, also its folder's name.

start.description: When the step started, ISO 8601 in UTC.

end.description: When it ended, ISO 8601 in UTC.
